findings.evidence: `<form>` … `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` - none of the three `<form>` tags in the document have an `action` attribute
findings.fix: Give each form an explicit action, or replace the submit buttons with anchor-style links to appropriate confirmation sections, matching how "Continue" and "Archive" already navigate via href.
findings.violation: Clicking any of these submit buttons triggers a default browser form submission (GET request reloading the current document) instead of navigating to a result/confirmation state, breaking the fragment-link navigation pattern used consistently everywhere else in the mockup.

findings.fix: Add visible label text (e.g. "Duplicate") or an icon, and wire it to a destination state (e.g. a new project row or confirmation) consistent with the other buttons/links.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text content (only an aria-label) and no href/target, so it renders as a blank, non-functional control unlike every other interactive element in the mockup.

findings.evidence: `Archive project` while a separate `#archive-confirm` section exists with its own cancel/confirm links but is never linked to from anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Change `project-settings-archive-link`'s href to `#archive-confirm` so the confirmation screen is reachable before archiving.
findings.violation: The confirmation dialog ("Archive this project?") is unreachable dead content; the actual archive link skips straight to the final archived state, bypassing the confirmation step the document was clearly designed to have.
